items.title: Should Qualcomm Stockholders Worry About Its Shrinking Revenue?
items.summary: Qualcomm (QCOM) grew revenue just 1.9% over the last twelve months, against a compound pace of about 6.2% a year over five years and 4.5% over three. The quarterly path is worse. Across the last four quarters, year-over-year growth slid from 10.0% to 5.0%, then to declines of 3.5% and 4.0%. That turn to shrinking quarterly sales is the risk to weigh.

items.title: Ciena's Backlog Or Arista's Margins: Which Should Carry Your AI Network Bet?
items.summary: If you own Ciena (CIEN) or Arista Networks, you own one idea: AI is driving fast growth in network traffic, and both sell the equipment that carries it. Both raised their revenue outlooks in their latest reports, and both say they could ship more if supply loosened. Then the pair splits. Ciena's case rests on orders it cannot yet fill, while Arista already keeps about 43 cents of every sales dollar as operating profit.

items.title: Marvell Rises 5% as Piper Sandler Starts Coverage With $270 Target; Broadcom Edges Higher, NVIDIA Holds Steady
items.summary: Piper Sandler just put a fresh bullish stamp on Marvell with a new price target, and CEO Matt Murphy is calling the company the Switzerland of AI silicon. Whether that neutrality is a strength or a liability ahead of a high-stakes October roadmap event is the real question.

items.title: The Better Nvidia Killer: Broadcom or AMD?
items.summary: Broadcom and AMD both posted explosive AI growth and both have hyperscalers locked in as customers, but only one makes a convincing case for actually unseating Nvidia as the king of AI compute.

items.title: The Next Growth Cycle Could Take Qualcomm to New Highs
items.summary: Qualcomm's handset business is shrinking while its automotive and data center ambitions are scaling fast, and the tension between those two forces will determine whether the stock revisits its highs or stalls out entirely.
